entries.clue: Highest in command initially skirts the issues (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: tells you to take the first letter of each of the words it follows

blocks.note: first letters of in, command, skirts

annotation.surface: A senior officer dodges the awkward questions.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'skirts' as a verb meaning avoids, but it only lends its S; 'initially' reaches back over three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the subjects on the table at a meeting are its issues.

entries.clue: Audio kit packeted ham-fistedly (4,4)

annotation.surface: Someone has clumsily boxed up their stereo equipment.
annotation.walkthrough: An odd word like 'packeted' is usually there for its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A tape deck is a piece of audio equipment for playing cassettes.

entries.clue: Kind of tense, drive over island for meat (8)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, RAM sits above I

annotation.surface: A stressed driver crosses to an island in search of food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kind of tense' reads as nervous, but it is grammar: the past tense.
annotation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a seasoned, smoked beef.

entries.clue: Everyman, perhaps mad, drew otters dancing (9,6)

indicatorNotes.dancing: letters that dance move around into a new order

annotation.surface: The setter, a bit unhinged, has been sketching otters at a dance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like part of the anagram signal, but it is the angry sense, CROSS. The setter names himself as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Everyman is the pen name of the person who sets this crossword.

entries.clue: Set point – fantastic – let's pick up the pace (4,2,2)

indicatorNotes.fantastic: fantastic = fanciful, so the letters take a fanciful new shape

annotation.surface: A tennis player at set point urges more speed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' reads as the player's cheer, not an instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from driving: pressing the accelerator pedal down, so a call to go faster.

entries.clue: Even movement of the ocean reported (4)

indicatorNotes.reported: what is reported is spoken, so we go by sound

blocks.note: the tide is the ocean's rise and fall

annotation.surface: A news item about calm, regular tides.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adjective describing the movement; it is the definition, as in a tied score.
annotation.definitionFit: A tied match is even, neither side ahead.

entries.clue: Carton half open, reptiles scurrying: nasty thing to receive in the mail (6-3,6)

annotation.definition: nasty thing to receive in the mail

indicatorNotes.half: 'half' asks for only one of the word's two equal parts, here the back three letters
indicatorNotes.scurrying: letters that scurry about end up in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone opens a parcel and snakes scuttle out: a horrible delivery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Open' reads as a description of the box but is plain fodder. Either half of CARTON could be meant; only TON fits the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: an anonymous letter full of spite is exactly the post nobody wants.

entries.clue: Drinks slowly in harbours (6)

blocks.note: to nurse a drink is to make it last
to nurse a grudge is to harbour it

annotation.surface: Someone sips drinks at the dockside pubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harbours' pretends to be the noun, places for ships; it is the verb, to keep a feeling alive.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses mean holding on to something and making it last.

entries.clue: The Ivy's serving tripe – but only starters, I believe (6)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is what a theist says, standing for the believer

indicatorNotes.only starters: only the first letter of each word is served

blocks.note: first letters of Ivy's, serving, tripe

annotation.surface: A diner is sure the smart restaurant is serving rubbish but has only tried the starters.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ivy is a well-known London restaurant, and 'starters' plays on the first course. 'The' is kept whole, so the first letters come only from the next three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A theist is someone who says 'I believe' in God.

entries.clue: Clergyman rejected nonsense by idiot (6)

indicatorNotes.rejected: rejected = thrown back, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A vicar dismisses a fool's foolish talk.
annotation.walkthrough: ROTSAP turned round reads PASTOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation.

entries.clue: Taunt accepted by Dad in France, English being distinguished (8)

indicatorNotes.accepted by: what is accepted by someone is taken in, so the taunt goes inside the father
indicatorNotes.in France: use the French word for Dad

annotation.surface: A French father puts up with teasing about his English airs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pedigree' works as an adjective, as in a pedigree dog, which is how it matches 'distinguished'.
annotation.definitionFit: Something pedigree has a distinguished, well-recorded lineage.

entries.clue: Loading area in which you might go bust (7)

annotation.definition2: in which you might go bust

blocks.note: a floating landing stage where boats load

blocks.clueFragment: in which you might go bust
blocks.note: a card game: in British twenty-one (blackjack), going over 21 is going bust

annotation.surface: A warehouse bay where a business might fail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go bust' reads as bankruptcy; in the card game it means exceeding 21.
annotation.definitionFit: A pontoon is both a floating jetty and the card game twenty-one.

entries.clue: No, I engendered flipping contempt (8)

indicatorNotes.flipping: flipped over, the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: Someone angrily denies fathering anything, with a mild British swear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' is a mild British oath, which is why it sits so naturally before 'contempt'. NOISIRED backwards gives DERISION.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mockery that shows scorn for its target.

entries.clue: Sleep with partners in largish numbers (6)

blocks.note: North and South are partners at bridge

annotation.surface: A racy line about sleeping around on a large scale.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests promiscuity; the partners are the bridge pair North and South.
annotation.definitionFit: Dozens means a fair-sized quantity.

entries.clue: Parts of beans that are used for worship (7)

blocks.note: bean is slang for head, so these are parts of the head: the flat sides above the cheekbones
buildings of worship, especially non-Christian ones

annotation.surface: Some beans are set aside for religious use.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beans' are heads here, from the slang 'use your bean'.
annotation.definitionFit: Temples are both the flat sides of the head and places of worship.

entries.clue: Refuse to camp: hope for resort and welcoming spa at the outset (7,4)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is a pile of refuse rather than refuse itself

indicatorNotes.welcoming: the jumbled letters take S in
indicatorNotes.at the outset: take only the first letter of spa

annotation.surface: Someone declines a camping trip, hoping for a holiday resort with a spa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb, to decline; it is the noun, rubbish. 'Resort' hides re-sort.
annotation.definitionFit: A compost heap is a pile of garden and kitchen refuse left to rot.

entries.clue: Institute enshrined in the law finally validates insurance documents (8)

indicatorNotes.enshrined in: something enshrined is placed within a shrine, so the I is set inside the law
indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of validates

annotation.surface: A legally recognised institute approves insurance paperwork.
annotation.walkthrough: The I goes in near the end: POLIC-I-E, then S.
annotation.definitionFit: Insurance policies are the contracts setting out cover.

entries.clue: Got to camp (8)

blocks.note: a sad film that got to you moved or influenced you

annotation.surface: Someone finally reached the campsite.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words change their part of speech: 'got to' is moved emotionally, and 'camp' is the adjective, theatrically mannered.
annotation.definitionFit: Affected means both emotionally moved and artificially showy.

entries.clue: Delivering while almost asleep (8,3)

annotation.definitionNote: 'almost asleep' describes the state of dropping off rather than being the phrase itself

blocks.note: leaving a parcel at someone's door

annotation.surface: A tired courier is nodding off on the round.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is one exhausted delivery driver; the two halves are simply two senses of the same phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: To drop off is both to deliver and to fall asleep.

entries.clue: Cowboys use these in Dallas so sparingly (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Dallas, through so, into the start of sparingly

annotation.surface: Texan cowboys hardly ever use them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sparingly' seems to comment on how often; it just supplies the final S.
annotation.definitionFit: A lasso is a cowboy's looped rope for catching cattle.

entries.clue: Exercise in the gym? Don't look so sad (4-2)

blocks.note: pulling yourself up to a bar until your face clears it
a stock phrase of encouragement: lift your head

annotation.surface: A trainer tells a gloomy gym-goer to cheer up.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen belongs to the exercise; the encouragement is usually written as two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Chin-up names both a pull-up exercise and the phrase of encouragement.

entries.clue: More painful part of stomach, i.e. reticulum (6)

indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of stomach, through i.e., into the first letter of reticulum

annotation.surface: A vet explains that the cow's reticulum hurts more than the rest of its stomach.
annotation.walkthrough: The reticulum is one of a cow's four stomach chambers, which makes the anatomy look genuine.
annotation.definitionFit: The comparative of achy: aching more, so more painful.

entries.clue: When irritated, interfere after rector's left one of the Canaries (8)

indicatorNotes.When irritated: stirred up, the letters get jumbled
indicatorNotes.left: the R has left, so drop it

blocks.note: the word before its R is removed

annotation.surface: An annoyed rector stops meddling and flies off to the Canary Islands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canaries' looks like birds; it means the Canary Islands. Only one of INTERFERE's two Rs goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Tenerife is the largest of the Canary Islands.

entries.clue: Up to now, Romeo not seen in comfy spot (4)

indicatorNotes.not seen: the R is no longer seen, so it drops out

blocks.note: a two-word phrase meaning until this moment
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: Romeo hasn't been spotted on the couch yet.
annotation.walkthrough: Romeo reads as the lover; here he is only the letter R.
annotation.definitionFit: A sofa is a comfortable place to sit.

entries.clue: Something African National Congress tabled in opposing Nationalists, primarily? (8)

annotation.definition: Something African National Congress tabled in opposing Nationalists, primarily?

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the prime, first, letter of each word

blocks.clueFragment: Something African National Congress tabled in opposing Nationalists
blocks.note: first letters of the eight words

annotation.surface: The ANC proposed a measure against the apartheid-era Nationalist government.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the recipe and the definition: sanctions against the Nationalist regime were what the ANC urged.
annotation.definitionFit: A sanction is a penalty imposed against a state, like those the ANC sought against apartheid South Africa.

entries.clue: Punctilious Detective Inspector leaves area (6)

indicatorNotes.leaves: DI leaves the word, so drop it

annotation.surface: A fussy police inspector walks off the patch.
annotation.walkthrough: The area must be named first; only DISTRICT begins with DI.
annotation.definitionFit: Punctilious means strict about fine detail.

entries.clue: Fantastic Island that can be seen in comics (8)

annotation.definition: that can be seen in comics
annotation.definitionNote: a descriptive phrase standing for the comic-book hero

blocks.note: the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland

annotation.surface: A wonderful island that turns up in comic books.
annotation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, so 'Island' clues MAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Superman is the classic comic-book superhero.

entries.clue: In the East End, he got up and wiped out? (6)

indicatorNotes.In the East End: Cockneys of London's East End drop their Hs, so HE becomes 'E

blocks.note: he raised, with the H dropped

annotation.surface: A Cockney stood up and was exhausted.
annotation.walkthrough: The East End is London's traditionally Cockney district, where the H of 'he' is dropped. 'Wiped out' reads as exhausted; it means rubbed out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rubbed out, as a pencil mark or a recording is.
